chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Uncles Louis, Lucien and Willie and the pride in music
summary: Danny names uncles Louis Barbarin with Celestin, Lucien the showman drummer, and Willie on trumpet, in a family proud of music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, out of Chicago. It was a fantastic act. Then I asked my Uncle Louis. He's in New Orleans. He's with Papa Celestin, Sidney Desvignes, and he's probably one of the best young drummers. And I got my other Uncle Lucien, he was a drummer, he played in ballrooms, he played in honky-tonks, played at house parties everywhere. He got... They said Lucien's got more personality than all of them. He'd play a street parade. He'd play for advertising on a truck, he'd get out of the truck with his cymbal in the street, and go play all up and down the street in front of people's buildings.
Just a stick and a cymbal, huh.

Yeah. He was a showman. And he'd create a big scene in the street. And I got Willie, he's about two years older than me, he's trying to play trumpet. And he's playing with the little band. Everybody's playing music.
Estee Bijou, who was a great vaudeville performer -- she was a cousin of my grandfather. And all of them...

You were entangled all around music. And everybody's proud. Ain't nobody to tell you, "Don't fool with no music." They're saying, "Yeah, so-and-so is doing wonderful with the music." It's encouraging...
...to get somewhere, to get any esteem.
That's beautiful, Danny. This is unbelievable.
